analysis.investment_thesis: Aurionpro is a decent capital-light software business with improving ROIC (~18%) and strong recent revenue growth, but at an earnings yield of ~5% it fails the Magic Formula's cheapness test and does not meet the buy threshold. Until the valuation compresses, the margin of safety is insufficient for a systematic value purchase.
key_strengths: Near-zero leverage (D/E 0.02, net cash ~INR 239 Cr) with 5/5 years of positive OCF gives balance-sheet resilience
Revenue and EBIT on a clear upswing — revenue +32% YoY in FY2025, EBIT CAGR 10% over 9 years with expanding margins
Operating margin expanding to 17.4% and ROCE at 18.1% shows the core fintech-software business earns above cost of capital
key_risks: Earnings yield ~5% (EBIT INR 242 Cr / EV ~INR 4,855 Cr) is well below the Magic Formula's 12%+ threshold — stock is priced for perfection
FY2025 FCF (INR 62 Cr) is only 33% of net profit (INR 188 Cr) with capex surging to INR 95 Cr and investing outflows of INR 421 Cr, signaling aggressive acquisition-led growth with uncertain returns
Promoter stake at a low 26.88% reduces alignment, and the FY2021 large write-down (-INR 192 Cr net profit, -INR 118 Cr 'other income') raises historic capital-allocation concerns
red_flags: Earnings yield of ~5% fails Magic Formula minimum threshold of 12%
FCF-to-net-profit conversion collapsed to ~33% in FY2025; heavy acquisition spending (INR 421 Cr investing outflows) may dilute future ROIC
FY2021 goodwill/impairment-driven loss of INR -192 Cr — a reminder that management has made costly capital misallocation before
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on Aurionpro: EBIT FY2025 = INR 242 Cr; EV = Market Cap (INR 5,094 Cr) + Debt (INR 30 Cr) – Cash (INR 269 Cr) = ~INR 4,855 Cr. Earnings yield = 242/4,855 = ~5.0% — well below the 12% threshold where Greenblatt begins to find stocks attractive. ROIC, proxied by reported ROCE of 18.1%, is decent but below the 25%+ level that signals a truly exceptional business moat. On both axes of the Magic Formula — cheapness AND quality — Aurionpro falls into mediocre territory, earning neither a standout cheap valuation nor an elite return-on-capital profile.

The business trajectory is genuinely improving: operating income has grown from INR 84 Cr (FY2021) to INR 242 Cr (FY2025), finance costs are falling, and the balance sheet is essentially debt-free. However, the FY2025 investing outflow of INR 421 Cr (acquisitions/capex) and a financing inflow of INR 283 Cr (likely equity raise) indicate management is diluting and deploying capital aggressively — exactly the serial-acquirer behavior that can destroy ROIC over time. The P/E of 25x and EV/EBITDA of 18.4x offer no margin of safety. The stock is a fair business at a full price; it enters buy territory only if EV/EBIT falls toward 8–9x (implying a ~35–40% price decline from current levels).
